She argues that while AI can feel easier, smoother, and less demanding, it removes the very tension that makes relationships meaningful. The talk reminds us that conflict, challenge, and imperfection are not flaws in relationships, but part of their beauty. Anna Ekblom is a public speaker and communication expert with nearly ten years of experience helping individuals master the psychology of human connection. Speaking on perception, connection, and social intelligence, she has delivered keynotes across Europe, bringing psychological science to life in ways that deepen relationships and transform communication. With a Master’s degree in psychology and a Bachelor’s degree in rhetoric, Anna shares insights with a broad audience on TikTok and is a frequent guest on podcasts and interviews. description: My generation may be the first that needs protection not only from wrong answers, but from perfect ones. When AI gives students polished answers before we have tested, questioned, or struggled with our own ideas, it can create the feeling of understanding before real thinking has begun. This talk reveals what we may lose when answers arrive too early — and offers a simple way to keep human judgment in the lead. Anthony Feng is a Chinese student speaker, homeschool learner, and co-founder of IgnisMinds Academy, a future-oriented learning project exploring education in the age of AI. Having spent many years in a self-directed learning environment, he has been involved in building a local AI learning companion and thinking about how young people can learn with technology without losing their own judgment. description: We’re taught to connect the dots as children to see patterns, make meaning, and understand the bigger picture. It’s rewarded as curiosity, celebrated as learning, and framed as the simplest path to clarity: a puzzle with a right answer. But somewhere along the way, we stop. The ideas already exist scattered across people, silos, and experiences. The real gap is not creation, but connection. And what prevents that connection is not scarcity of insight, but the discomfort of what emerges when patterns are seen across boundaries. In organizations, connecting the dots is no longer about solving a simple puzzle. It becomes an act of Intrapreneurship. Intrapreneurs are not defined by title or authority, but by perception the ability to see across systems, recognize patterns others miss, and connect dots that were never meant to be viewed together. They reveal what the organization already knows, but has not yet been able to see as a whole Dr. Chitra Anand is an award-winning transformation
title: Why organizations fail to innovate | Dr. Chitra Anand | TEDxLakeheadU

description: This talk challenges the comforting belief that “good people” and “criminals” are fundamentally different, arguing instead that the line between them is a gradual slope we all stand on. Drawing on psychological research, it reveals how small moral compromises and diffused responsibility can lead ordinary individuals to cause harm. Ultimately, it offers practical guardrails to resist this slide, showing that integrity is built through conscious choices about who we are becoming. description: This talk reframes embarrassment as a signal of growth rather than something to avoid, arguing that the moments we most want to escape often point directly to who we want to become. Blending personal experience with psychology, it shows how the “spotlight effect” and fear of judgment hold us back, even though most people are paying far less attention than we think. By intentionally seeking small, awkward moments and embracing imperfection, we can build confidence, connection, and a more authentic version of ourselves. Kelly is a Hong Kong-born digital strategist working at the intersection of AI and human experience. Currently completing an MSc in AI and Emerging Technologies for Management at Hong Kong Polytechnic University, she holds a BSc in Art and Technology from the University of Oregon. Her work spans AI research, GenAI workflow design, and creative strategy across academic and commercial settings. Her belief that technology and craft are not opposites earned her a Gold Award

description: As the healthcare system buckles under the weight of physician shortages and burnout, Artificial Intelligence is no longer just an optional tool—it is a desperate necessity. But as AI shifts from being a simple "assistant" to an autonomous "agent" executing complex medical workflows, we are quietly shifting massive responsibility to machines. We must stop asking "Where can we put AI?" and start asking "Where must we keep a human?" before it is too late. James McCormack is a Thunder Bay born founder and applied AI practitioner. He holds a computer science background from Lakehead University and began his healthcare AI work at the Thunder Bay Regional Health Research Institute, contributing to research on next generation electronic medical records, computerized physician order entry, and clinical data systems. His research spanned stroke care, hospitalist medicine, internal medicine, oncology, and nephrology. He is also an alumnus of Harvard Medical School and the MIT Health Innovation
title: The human cost of AI in healthcare | James McCormack | TEDxLakeheadU

Diana enjoys reading, theatre, public speaking, debate, creative expression, and observing the hidden emotional messages in everyday learning environments. The talk closes with a simple challenge: replace “I can’t” with “yet,” and take one brave step toward becoming who you are still in the process of creating. Dr. Damien Tomaselli is a South African born creator-scholar exploring narrative across film, gaming, virtual reality, and emerging media.
